title: Saffire I-III Large-Scale Flame Growth Overview
content: Conducted inside uncrewed Cygnus cargo spacecraft.Saffire-I burned a large 0.4m x 1.0m cotton-fiberglass sample, proving large fires can grow indefinitely in microgravity without buoyant convection. Saffire-II tested 9 material strips (Nomex, PMMA, Mylar) showing lower ignition delays. Saffire-III evaluated high forced flow velocities (~20 cm/s), proving higher airspeeds accelerate flame spread.

title: Saffire IV-VI Advanced Exploration & Cleanup
content: Focused on Artemis lunar/Mars habitats. Tested elevated O2 concentrations up to 30% and reduced cabin pressure (8.2 psi). Higher O2 drastically reduced ignition delay and increased temperatures. Saffire-VI tested catalytic 'Smoke Eater' scrubbers converting toxic CO to CO2 with ~70% efficiency.

title: Materials Flammability & Limiting Oxygen Concentration (LOC)
content: NASA-STD-6001 1g tests are non-conservative in microgravity. Nomex/Ultem form protective char layers (Low/Mod risk). PMMA is a non-charring vaporizing fuel (High risk). Mylar is a thermoplastic that melts without dripping, retaining fuel in the flame zone and dropping its Limiting Oxygen Concentration (LOC) critically low.

title: Fire Behavior Across Gravity Levels
content: Microgravity (0g) creates round, soot-rich diffusion flames dependent on ventilation. Lunar gravity (0.16g) creates weak buoyancy with wider flammability limits for charring fuels like Nomex. Martian gravity (0.38g) allows propagation while retaining molten fuel in the reaction zone.

title: Ventilation Airflow Speed Effects
content: Quiescent (0 cm/s) fires self-extinguish due to O2 starvation and CO2 buildup. Low flow (2-10 cm/s) sustains steady microgravity burning. High flow (15-30 cm/s) increases spread rate up to blow-off limits. Turning off ventilation is a key immediate suppression tactic.

title: Spacecraft Fire Detection Sensors & Signatures
content: Optical smoke detectors target sub-micron aerosols (PM1 < 1 um). Rapid Carbon Monoxide (CO) spikes are the earliest and most reliable chemical indicator of incipient fires. Thermal radiometers detect infrared radiation before visible flames appear.

title: Toxic Combustion Gas Dynamics & Scrubbing
content: Primary toxins include Carbon Monoxide (CO), Carbon Dioxide (CO2), and Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN). Spacecraft scrubbers must remove CO and fine particulates prior to crew removing emergency respirators. Saffire scrubbers successfully converted 157g of toxic CO to CO2.

title: Fire Safety in Artemis & Mars Habitats
content: Exploration atmospheres favor lower pressure (8.2 psi) and higher oxygen (30% O2) to streamline EVA pre-breathe. Elevated O2 expands flammable material categories, lowers ignition thresholds, and increases heat release rates, requiring strict material screening.

title: Microgravity Fire Suppression Strategies
content: Suppression relies on CO2 extinguishers (requiring crew breathing masks), fine water mist, or nitrogen flooding. Extinction occurs via thermal cooling, diluting O2 below LOC, or shutting down cabin airflow ducts to immediately starve flames.

title: Saffire Flight Hardware Architecture
content: Flow duct modules measure ~53x90x133 cm. Equipped with thermocouples, radiometers, flow anemometers, and high-speed video cameras to track temperature profiles, air velocities, and flame front behavior ignited by high-resistance wire strips.
